svg.text: Proto shield - what each part does, and how the current flows
Six panels, one per path the current takes. In each picture only that path's parts and wires are in colour; everything else is grey. Top row: a 3/4 view and the view straight down;
below: the underside (flipped top-over-bottom, USB end still left). The panels light up one after another (30 s loop). Pictures are renders of the INTENDED build, not photos.

g.text: The 2S pack (7.2-8.4 V) arrives through the fuse, BMS and rocker at J5's VBAT pin and
the VBAT strip; w1 carries it to the TB6612's motor-power pin VM, where C1 and C2 hold
it steady. The divider's top resistor (R100k) also taps it, so the Uno can measure the
The LM2596 on the deck makes about 5 V from VBAT and brings it in on J5's +5V2 pin. A
bridge bus along row P4 spreads it to the encoder (J1), both LED strips (J3, J4) and,
through w4, JP1's bottom pin - used only if the servo jumper is moved down.
Logic 5V (the Uno, from the Pi's USB)
JP1 top two pins + the jumper cap
The Pi's USB powers the Uno; the Uno's 5V pin is rail V. w3 takes it to the TB6612's
logic supply (VCC), and JP1's cap on the top two pins passes it to the servo's V+ on
D11 PWM, D8 + D12 direction, D10 enable -> TB6612
D6 / D5 -> LED data (J3, J4), 400 ohm in each wire
D2 / D3 <- encoder (straight to the Uno)
The Uno runs the firmware: it reads the Pi's commands and drives the pins. Dupont leads
carry its signals: speed, direction and enable to the TB6612, the servo angle, the LED
data. It reads the pack voltage on A0 (VBAT / 9.33 from the divider) and the encoder on
D2 / D3, which plug straight into the Uno.
TB6612 AO1+BO1 and AO2+BO2 (paralleled on the carrier)
The TB6612 switches VBAT into the motor. Its A and B channels are paralleled on the
carrier for more current, and two bridges take M1 / M2 to J1 and on to the N20 motor.
Speed comes from PWM, direction from the DIR pins.
Every current comes back to ground, and all grounds meet at one point: rail B, the
star. The TB6612 returns through w2, the servo through w5, the headers' GND pins
through their bridges; the LM2596's ground arrives on J6 (wire W13).
